notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Small cylindrical white bollards with a black base, sometimes with a yellow reflector or a flat shape. Found nowhere else.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Most utility poles are octagonal concrete, often with engravings on the side.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Stop signs say "ALTO".

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Short plates in a huge variety of designs; front plates are required.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: White solid edge lines with a single unbroken yellow centre line; broken or double yellow centres also occur.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: National highway shield has a curvy outline with the country name on top; state roads have a straight border with state initials.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs use a very large all-caps white font, and arrows are noticeably thick.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Kilometre markers are white with black text and a black outline.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Yellow accents on kerbs and bridge barriers are common.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Wide cylindrical black or white water tanks sit on rooftops.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: OXXO and Pemex are the common shop and fuel brands; US pickup trucks are popular.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Many place names come from an indigenous language: lots of x and tl, endings like -tlan and -ec.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Circular electricity meters are used.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: One of few Latin American countries with Generation 2 coverage; Generation 3 cars have a stubby coiled antenna or a long red brake light.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Cacti of many species are extremely common.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Prickly pear with flat oval pads is common in the centre and rare in the south and coast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Vast blue agave fields for tequila, mostly in Jalisco and Nayarit.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Giant cardon cacti with many arms and ribbed trunks are very common on the Baja peninsula.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Saguaro and organ pipe cacti are found in Sonora.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Alien-looking boojum trees grow almost only in southern Baja.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tree-like yuccas are common around San Luis Potosí and Zacatecas.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Sugar cane is found everywhere but is by far most common in Veracruz.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Blindingly white soil on the Yucatán peninsula, strongest in Quintana Roo; only reliable in Generation 3.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Short, stunted pine forests on rocky mountains in western Chihuahua and Durango.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Red brick buildings cluster in Jalisco, Michoacán, Guanajuato and Aguascalientes.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Mud brick houses are most abundant in Durango and dry desert states.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Northern houses look like pastel bungalows, gated with front yards and orange tiles.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Thatched roofs are most common on the Yucatán peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosí.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Some Jalisco bollards carry a crown and the state name, the only bollards with writing.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Concrete poles with insulators hanging below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatán peninsula.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are found around the capital and in Hidalgo and Morelos.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with a mesh body are found mostly in San Luis Potosí, Guanajuato and Querétaro.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: White centre lines are most common in Tabasco.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line is seen in Sinaloa, Durango and Guerrero.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: A thick cross is painted on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Taxis around the capital have a white lower half and a pink upper half.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Irregular cobblestone is common in central states, most of all in Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Querétaro.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Hexagonal tile paving appears in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
